summary: auth-service began returning 401 invalid_token on ~36% of POST /v1/token/validate calls at 14:02 UTC on 2026-04-15; api-gateway propagated ~21% 5xx upstream. Two changes landed 1-2 minutes earlier — deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, jjwt 0.11→0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten) at 14:00 and config change cfg-2705 (JWT signing-key rotation k-2025-10→k-2026-04) at 14:01. All resource/infra metrics are flat and neither change has been rolled back, so there is no rollback evidence to discriminate. Both the deploy and the key rotation match historical analogues (HIST-109 bad_deployment; HIST-108 config_change) and the ~1/3 partial failure rate is consistent with either. auth-service logs are unsearchable (log backend 503), removing the decisive evidence. Outcome: inconclusive between bad_deployment (JWT library upgrade) and config_change (signing-key rotation); the root cause is one of these two auth-service changes.

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT library upgrade (dep-5710 v7.3.0) introduced a token-validation bug
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The auth-service deploy dep-5710 at 14:00 replaced the token parser (jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12, 'breaking parser API') and rewrote TokenValidator, causing ~1/3 of valid tokens to be rejected as invalid_token starting 14:02. Exact analogue of HIST-109 (JWT library upgrade changed validation default -> 401 invalid_token).

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 deployed 14:00 with breaking JWT parser change
validation failures surface as 401 invalid_token at gateway
resource metrics flat, so failure is in validation logic not resources

assumptions: The log-pipeline outage (F11) hides the auth-service-side stack trace that would name the failing component
A 14:02 onset 1-2 min after a 14:00 deploy is consistent with rollout completion
Neither change was reverted (F17), so the absence of rollback recovery is not evidence against this hypothesis

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) invalidated tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 at 14:01 switched jwt.signing.key_id to k-2026-04; a subset of pods/tokens still on the old key id (k-2025-10) were rejected, producing ~1/3 invalid_token starting 14:02. Exact analogue of HIST-108 (key rotation before all pods loaded the new key).

causal_chain.claim: only a fraction of validations fail (~1/3), consistent with partial key propagation

assumptions: Key rotation propagates via config push on a ~1-min cycle reaching 14:02
A stable ~1/3 failure fraction reflects a fixed subset of pods/tokens on the stale key
The rotation was not accompanied by a JWKS pre-publish step

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / capacity saturation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service ran out of CPU/memory/connections or was saturated by load, causing errors.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cpu_pct (~38%), memory_pct (~52%), latency_p99 (~90ms) and restarts (0) are all flat across onset (F7); request_rate is steady ~400 req/s with no surge (F8); redis hit_ratio ~96% and user-db connections flat (F9, F10).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Dependency or infrastructure failure (redis-cache / user-db / kyc-provider)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A downstream datastore or the external kyc-provider failed, causing token validation errors.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: redis-cache hit_ratio stays ~96% with no eviction or memory step change (F9); user-db connections flat (F10); logs show 401 invalid_token (an auth decision), not upstream timeouts/5xx (F5).

facts.statement: auth-service error rate was ~0.2% through 14:00 then jumped to 37.21% at 14:02.
The error rate stayed ~35-38% continuously to 15:59 with no recovery.
Deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten) completed 14:00 and is not rolled back.
Config change cfg-2705 rotated jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01.
api-gateway error rate rose 0.24% -> 21% at the 14:02 bucket.
auth-service CPU, memory, latency and restarts are flat across onset.
auth-service request rate and rate-limiting are unchanged across onset.
redis-cache hit ratio, evictions and memory show no step change.
Past incidents HIST-109 (JWT library upgrade) and HIST-108 (signing key rotation) both show 401 invalid_token on auth-service.
The failure is partial (~1/3), not total.

assumptions: The 14:02 onset (1-2 min after both changes) is equally consistent with deploy rollout completion and config propagation.
A stable ~1/3 failure fraction reflects a partial subset (pods/tokens) rather than a random logic error.
Historical incidents HIST-109/HIST-108 are plausible leads, not proof of the current cause.

timeline.event: Last normal bucket: auth-service error_rate 0.21%, gateway 0.24%
Deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, JWT lib 0.11->0.12, TokenValidator rewritten) completes
Config change cfg-2705 rotates JWT signing key id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04
auth-service error_rate jumps to ~37%; gateway error_rate to ~21% and first 401 invalid_token logged at 14:02:22
Incident still ongoing; error rate ~36-38%, no rollback performed

recommended_actions.action: Retrieve auth-service application logs from the identity namespace once the log pipeline is restored (or via a pod-level tail) to see the exact validation failure reason.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the single piece of missing evidence that would separate the deploy from the key rotation (stack trace, key id used, clock-skew error).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back deploy dep-5710 to the previous version first (fastest, reversible) while leaving the key rotation in place; if error rate recovers, the deploy is the cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5710 is a higher-confidence analogue (HIST-109 same symptom+service) and is a cleanly reversible lever; a controlled rollback is itself a discriminating experiment.

recommended_actions.action: If rollback of the deploy does NOT recover, revert cfg-2705 (restore key id k-2025-10) or pre-publish the new JWKS to all pods and force a config reload.
recommended_actions.rationale: Tests the key-rotation hypothesis; HIST-108 shows the fix is republishing the previous key and staging rotations.

recommended_actions.action: Add auth-service-side metrics/log labels for validation failure reason (bad signature vs expired vs untrusted issuer/skew) and key id in use.
recommended_actions.rationale: Current telemetry aggregates all invalid_token failures, preventing discrimination between key and parser causes.

recommended_actions.action: Stage JWT signing-key rotations (pre-publish JWKS, drain old key) and decouple them from library upgrades; add a canary stage to auth-service deploys.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both trigger types have previously caused 401 outages (HIST-108, HIST-109); staggering changes removes this ambiguity.

data_gaps: auth-service application logs are unavailable (log backend returned 503, tc-021) — the namespace log-pipeline outage removes the decisive evidence (stack trace, key id, clock-skew vs signature error).
No rollback of either dep-5710 or cfg-2705 has occurred and the incident is still ongoing, so there is no rollback-recovery observation to attribute the fault.
No per-pod / per-replica breakdown of auth-service error rate is available, so a partial-fleet (stale-key or mixed-version) pattern cannot be confirmed vs a uniform logic bug.
api-gateway logs contain no key/JWKS-related lines (0 matches), so the key-id path is not directly observable.
kyc-provider has no telemetry, so its health could not be verified (though logs show 401 invalid_token, not provider timeouts).

findings.statement: auth-service error_rate was ~0.2% until 14:00 and jumped to 37.21% in the 14:02 bucket, last normal sample 14:00:00 = 0.21.
The auth-service error rate stayed elevated at ~35-38% continuously from 14:02 through 15:59 with no recovery (mean 32.85%, last 38.23%).

A code deployment dep-5710 for auth-service (v7.3.0, 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten') completed at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z and is still live with rolled_back_at null.
A config change cfg-2705 rotated auth-service jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z (author security-automation, 'Scheduled signing-key rotation').
api-gateway logged 466 WARN entries, all of the pattern 'auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token', first seen 2026-04-15T14:02:22Z.
api-gateway error_rate jumped from 0.24% in the 13:59 bucket to 21.06% in the 14:02 bucket, and stayed ~21% thereafter.
auth-service resource metrics are flat across the incident: cpu_pct ~36-42%, memory_pct ~46-58%, latency_p99_ms ~82-101ms, restarts 0 throughout.
auth-service request_rate was steady ~358-435 req/s before and after onset (no traffic surge); rate_limited_per_min stayed ~2/min.
Shared dependency redis-cache stayed healthy: hit_ratio_pct ~94-98%, evictions_per_min ~1.5-5, memory_pct ~60-77%, with no step change at onset.
user-db connections_active stayed flat (~22-27) across the window, no connection exhaustion.
auth-service logs could not be retrieved: query_logs returned 'backend unavailable (503) (gave up after 3 attempts)', confirming the log-pipeline outage noted in the incident report.

Historical incident HIST-109 (2025-07-11) is 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade' with symptoms '401 invalid_token','token validation failures', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default', category bad_deployment.

Historical incident HIST-108 (2025-10-01) is '401s after JWT signing key rotation' with symptoms '401 invalid_token','users logged out', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', category config_change.

auth-service depends on user-db (db), redis-cache (shared cache) and kyc-provider (external, has_telemetry false); api-gateway calls auth-service over HTTP — the fault path is gateway -> auth-service.
Failure fraction is partial, not total: auth-service error rate plateaued near 36% (~1/3) rather than ~100%, and gateway near 21%.
No log lines in api-gateway mention 'jwks' or signing 'key' during the window (0 matches for both filters).
Neither triggering change was rolled back and the incident is still ongoing at the latest data point (15:59), so no rollback-recovery evidence exists to attribute blame.
